$comment: Design tokens for Openfield. Every colour in `light` and `dark` was measured out of operator-supplied reference footage with tools/measure-frame.mjs -- see design/measurements.md for provenance and the scale caveat. Values marked `approx: true` were NOT measured and must not be presented as parity.

meta.scaleCaveat: Footage is macOS at unknown display scale inside a 1920x1080 video. Colours are exact; sizes are scale-relative and need validation on a Windows display.

bg.note: Corrected from #fdfdfc. Pure white. The previous value was a warm off-white sampled from compressed video, and chroma subsampling in the codec is precisely what turns a white page faintly cream. An off-white ground also lowers the contrast of every text token sitting on it, which is a side effect nobody chooses on purpose. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is the gate that actually constrains this value rather than taste.

bgSidebar.note: Corrected from #f4f2f0. Much closer to the ground than before. Ours sat ~13 steps below the page; a sidebar that reads as part of the window sits ~7. A wider gap makes the sidebar look like a second application pane rather than a region of this one. Cross-checked against a second open-source implementation of the same kind of product, which uses the same narrow relationship; the number here is chosen here. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is the gate that actually constrains this value rather than taste.

bgOverlay.note: Menus and dialogs are the brightest surface.

bgHover.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

bgSelected.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

bgActive.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

textMuted.note: Derived, not sampled. Raised from #9b9997 by walking lightness at the same hue and saturation until the worst background clears 4.5:1 (now 4.55:1, was 2.54:1). Section labels, column headers, menu descriptions and database cells. All reading material at 14-16px, so WCAG AA normal text applies. At 2.44:1 this was the dimmest thing on the page that anyone is meant to read. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is why this is not a hand-picked grey.

textFaint.note: Derived, not sampled. Raised from #c4c2c0 by walking lightness at the same hue and saturation until the worst background clears 3:1 (now 3.07:1, was 1.59:1). Block drag handle, disclosure chevrons, menu group labels and column counts. Affordances rather than prose, so the large-text 3:1 figure applies. Held below textMuted on purpose so the two tokens stay doing different jobs. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is why this is not a hand-picked grey.

accent.note: Placeholder accent, ours by design. Must not resemble any vendor mark.

danger.note: Used for the visually distinct Move to Trash action (operator requirement R2).

bgCode.note: Code and callout panels. These were faked with bgActive, which is right for a selected row and far too light for a code panel.

bgSunken.note: Recessed areas that hold other content, such as a board column. Distinct from bgCode: a sunken area is a container, not a panel.

bgBadge.note: Small counts and chips sitting on text. Tuned separately from the surfaces because it has to hold against body copy without competing with it.

gray.note: Text-colour palette for inline marks. Ours by design, not measured: the reference product's hues were not sampled, because sampling them would be copying its palette. Each passes 4.5:1 on bg in this theme (tools/check-contrast.mjs). The matching background is derived in CSS with color-mix, so one token per hue covers both.

bg.note: Measured from a native-resolution reference screenshot (2736x1482 at dpr 2) with tools/measure-screenshot.mjs. Supersedes an earlier value read off compressed video, which was too dark.

bgSidebar.note: Measured from two reference screenshots at 2x (analysis/ref/database-screenshot.png and analysis/ref/block-types.png): sidebar #202020 against page #191919. Supersedes a copy of the page colour that carried a note admitting the delta was unisolated.

bgHover.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

bgSelected.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

bgActive.note: An alpha overlay rather than a solid colour, so the same token composites correctly on any surface instead of needing one value per background.

text.note: Measured from a native-resolution reference screenshot (2736x1482 at dpr 2) with tools/measure-screenshot.mjs. Supersedes an earlier value read off compressed video. The gap is large: #f0efed against the #cacacb previously believed, because compression pulls near-white down and the eye cannot tell.

Section labels, column headers, menu descriptions and database cells. All reading material at 14-16px, so WCAG AA normal text applies. At 2.44:1 this was the dimmest thing on the page that anyone is meant to read. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is why this is not a hand-picked grey.

Block drag handle, disclosure chevrons, menu group labels and column counts. Affordances rather than prose, so the large-text 3:1 figure applies. Held below textMuted on purpose so the two tokens stay doing different jobs. Verified by tools/check-contrast.mjs, which is why this is not a hand-picked grey.

bgCode.note: Code and callout panels. These were faked with bgActive, which is right for a selected row and far too light for a code panel.

bgSunken.note: Recessed areas that hold other content, such as a board column. Distinct from bgCode: a sunken area is a container, not a panel.

gray.note: Dark-theme text colours. Lightened rather than reused: the light-theme hues sit at 4.5:1 on white and around 2:1 on #191919, which is unreadable. Each passes 4.5:1 on bg here (tools/check-contrast.mjs).

pageTop.note: Air above a page title. Deliberately not a step on the 4px scale: it is set by where the title should sit in the window, not by the block rhythm below it.

pageSide.note: Air beside the content measure. Less than the top, so the page reads as a column standing in space rather than a box.

pageTitleGap.note: Below the title, before the first block.

space.$comment: A 4px base scale. Only the small steps are pinned; larger rhythm steps are conventional rather than measured, and are tagged.

size.$comment: Scale-relative: measured from 1920-wide macOS footage in a 1920x1080 video. Validate on a Windows display before treating as final.

contentWidth.note: Measured from a native-resolution reference screenshot (2736x1482 at dpr 2) with tools/measure-screenshot.mjs. Right edge of the wrapped paragraph band. The previous 760px was an estimate roughly 135px too wide, which is the difference between comfortable reading and a long line of text.

menuMinWidth.note: Slash menu observed at this width.

type.$comment: Type sizes were NOT measured: the source is video, so glyph rasterisation would corrupt any measurement. These follow a conventional scale and are marked approximate until a native-resolution still is supplied.

title.note: Measured from a native-resolution reference screenshot (2736x1482 at dpr 2) with tools/measure-screenshot.mjs. Derived from ink-height ratios between bands, anchored to a 16px body.

h3.note: Measured from a native-resolution reference screenshot (2736x1482 at dpr 2) with tools/measure-screenshot.mjs. Derived from ink-height ratios between bands, anchored to a 16px body.

workspace.note: The workspace name in the sidebar header. The only type larger than body, and it earns it: it labels the whole tree the way a window title labels the window. Set to body-small it reads as one more row and the sidebar loses its top.

font.value: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

fontMono.value: 'Cascadia Code', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace

radius.$comment: Not measured. Conventional values for a document UI.

elevation.$comment: Shadows are layered: a tight contact shadow that grounds the surface and a wide ambient one that separates it from the page. One value cannot do both.

popover.note: Two layers: a tight contact shadow and a wide ambient one. A single value reads as a sticker rather than a lifted surface.

modal.note: Two layers: a tight contact shadow and a wide ambient one. A single value reads as a sticker rather than a lifted surface.

motion.$comment: NOT measured from the reference. Sensible defaults, all tagged approximate. Honour prefers-reduced-motion -- Motion's documented policy is reducedMotion: 'user'.
